Root cause on its worst document, itr-computation-with-slab-table (68.82 share@5): the PDF draws its last table past the bottom of its own sheet (rules at 848.4/866.8/885.2 on an 841.9 pt page, clipped by every viewer), the engine reproduced those rows, its model of the page needed 908 pt against an 841.8 pt budget, and the fitter answered the overrun with a GLOBAL squeeze (f=0.875) that came off every gap on the sheet including the top of the page - first paragraph w:before 1057 -> 392 twips, whole page 33.6 pt high, 65% of the ink invented and 69% of the source ink >5px from ours. Fix: DocxWriter.table() clips rows whose top edge is below the paper (keepRows) and cuts the straddling row at the edge (rowCapTw).
